chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Armstrong's foundling-home training and orphanage trumpeters
summary: Butler believes Armstrong learned rudiments and tonguing in the Waif's Home, like other orphanage-trained trumpeters such as Jabbo Smith and Gus Aikens, who knew solfeggio.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did you ever talk to Armstrong about trumpet playing?
Was he a very (unintelligible) what kind of knowledge did he have -- well, obviously he understood this, the way he played it.

Well, you see, I think he had to have the knowledge because he was in a foundling school, just like Jenkin's orphan, orphanage band. See, they teach them, their fellows, the rudiments of their trumpets. And all of them can tongue the horn and all of them got beautiful attacks. You catch all these trumpets (inaudible) coming out of them orphanage schools, they have attack. And they can double and triple

tongue it. They know their instrument. It's like we've got Cat Anderson, we had Jabbo Smith, we had another named Smith, all of them, Gus Aikens, all of them knew them instruments backwards. All of them knew solfeggio. And I think -- I'm sure Louis Armstrong would come under that same bracket.
